policies.lead: Who approves what, which day-2 actions are allowed, how long deployments live, how many and how large they may be, and how VMs are named.
policies.leadProject: Who approves what, which day-2 actions are allowed, how long deployments live and how many and how large they may be in your projects. You read the global policies and your projects', and write your projects' own unless an administrator set them.

enforcement.hard: Hard: it refuses, or waits for approval
enforcement.soft: Soft: it warns, and the requester may go on

policies.movesEveryone: It renumbers the policies of every project: set its priority instead
policies.name: Name

levels.rolesHint: Whoever holds one in the request's project when the level opens, themselves or through a group.
levels.managerHint: From the identity provider's manager claim. Without one, the level asks only its other approvers.

approval.title: Approval policies
approval.lead: Every policy that matches a request adds its levels of approvers, lower priority first.
approval.leadOwn: Every policy that matches a request adds its levels of approvers, lower priority first. You change your projects' own: they add levels to those of every project.
approval.sheetLead: Requests it applies to wait for each level's approvers, in order.
approval.autoHint: For example a small VM in dev: nobody needs to approve it
approval.emptyBody: Every request runs at once. Add a policy to have some approved first.
approval.removeLead: Requests stop waiting for {{approvers}} because of it.
approval.removeConsequences: Requests already waiting keep the approvals they were given. Another policy that matches still applies.

day2.title: Day-2 policies
day2.lead: The first policy that matches an action decides; when none does, the action is denied.
day2.leadOwn: The first policy that matches an action decides; when none does, the action is denied. You change your projects' own; a hard policy of every project that is stricter still wins.
day2.sheetLead: The first policy that matches an action decides whether it runs.
day2.enforcementHint: A soft policy's warning shows when the action is picked; the request keeps it.
day2.projectHint: A policy of every project that is hard and stricter still wins over a project's own.
day2.emptyBody: Every day-2 action is denied until a policy allows it.
day2.removeConsequences: Those actions are decided by the next policy that matches them, and denied when none does.

limits.title: Deployment limits
limits.lead: How many deployments each user or each project may have, and how much vCPU and memory each deployment may take. Each limit is decided on its own: the first policy by priority that sets it decides, and every hard global policy that sets it holds too.
limits.leadOwn: How many deployments each user or each project may have, and how much vCPU and memory each deployment may take. Each limit is decided on its own: the first policy by priority that sets it decides, and every hard global policy that sets it holds too. You change your projects' own.
limits.sheetLead: How many deployments each user or the project may have, and how large each may be. Leave a limit empty to leave it to other policies.
limits.projectHint: A project's policy only tightens a hard global one
limits.emptyBody: Users and projects may have as many deployments, each as large, as their quotas allow.
limits.emptyBodyAdd: Users and projects may have as many deployments, each as large, as their quotas allow. Add a policy to limit them.
limits.removeConsequences: New requests, updates and resizes meet the next policy that sets each limit, or none. Deployments that already pass a limit stay as they are.

lease.title: Lease policies
lease.lead: How long deployments live in each environment, and what happens when the lease ends. A lease rule that matches comes first.
lease.leadOwn: How long deployments live in each environment, and what happens when the lease ends. A lease rule that matches comes first. You change your projects' own, no looser than every project's.

expiry.power_off_then_delete: Power off, then delete after the grace period

lease.lifetimeHint: How long a deployment lives in all, from its creation. An extension past it needs approval. Empty for no limit
lease.enforcementHint: Soft: a longer lease, one more extension or one past the lifetime warns the requester instead of being refused or approved.
lease.sheetLead: How long deployments live in an environment, for every project or one; a project's own policy wins.
lease.projectHint: A project's own policy wins, but it can't be looser than every project's
lease.emptyBody: Deployments live until someone deletes them. Add a policy to give them a lease.
lease.removeConsequences: New deployments in {{environment}} get the lease every project has there, and extensions follow it. Deployments keep the lease they have.

rules.title: Lease rules
rules.lead: A lease for the deployments a condition matches, such as an item or a size. Rules are tried by priority before the lease policies, and the first that matches decides.
rules.leadOwn: A lease for the deployments a condition matches, such as an item or a size. Rules are tried by priority before the lease policies, and the first that matches decides. You change your projects' own, which give no more than what administrators set.
rules.sheetLead: A lease for the deployments its condition matches. Rules are tried by priority before the lease policies, and the first that matches decides.
rules.conditionHint: Reads what approval conditions read, for example {{first}} or {{second}}
rules.projectHint: A project admin's rule gives no more than what administrators set
rules.emptyBody: Every deployment gets its environment's lease, or its project's.
rules.emptyBodyAdd: Every deployment gets its environment's lease, or its project's. Add a rule to give some of them another one.
rules.removeLead: It stops giving its lease to the deployments where <mono>{{condition}}</mono>.
rules.removeConsequencesHeld: New requests get the next rule that matches them, or the lease policies. Deployments it decided follow the administrators' rule it was held to from now on, or else their project's or environment's lease.
rules.removeConsequences: New requests get the next rule that matches them, or the lease policies. Deployments it decided follow their project's or environment's lease from now on.

naming.title: Naming policies
naming.lead: The most specific offer wins over a blueprint's own template. A name is never given twice: rvav checks vCenter, DNS and every deployment it made.
naming.countedPolicy: From {{start}}, by {{increment}}, one for the policy
naming.wholeNumber: Enter a whole number, such as 1.
naming.sheetLead: It names the VMs of the items, projects and environments it is offered to.
naming.startHint: A counter in use goes on from its last number
naming.emptyBody: Each blueprint's own template names its VMs. Add a policy to name them the same way everywhere.
naming.removeConsequences: Offered to {{offers}}. They get the next policy that is offered to them, or their blueprint's own template. VMs keep the names they have.

quotas.allLead: What every project's deployments and requests not yet done may take together, beside each project's quota.
quotas.allEmpty: rvav as a whole may take any amount.
quotas.eachLead: What each user may hold in all projects together: the deployments they own and their requests not yet done. A request made for someone counts for them.
quotas.eachEmpty: Each user may take what their projects have left.

explain.title: What applies here
explain.lead: Which policies a request or a day-2 action would meet, and why. Nothing is changed.
explain.inputsHint: What lease rules and approval conditions read

quota.sheetLead: Requests that would pass a limit are refused, or need an approval.
quota.twin: This resource has a limit already: change that one.
quota.emptyAdd: {{empty}} Add a limit on vCPU, memory, storage or VMs.
quota.removeLead: Requests are no longer held to it.
quota.removeConsequences: The other levels' limits still apply.

member.title: Each member's quota
member.lead: What each member may hold in the project: the deployments they own and their requests not yet done. A request made for someone counts for them.
member.label: Limits for each member
member.empty: Each member may take what the project has left.

infra.lead: What blueprints' template and size pickers offer, the subnet each network deploys into, rvav's own IP ranges, and the tags of vCenter objects.
infra.label: Label

source.lead: Its template in each vCenter. VMs go to the clusters of these vCenters only, cloned from that vCenter's.
source.libraryHint: When it is an item of one

constraints.lead: Added to the item's, separated by commas: <mono>rvav-os/rhel9</mono>, <mono>!rvav-zone/pci</mono>, <mono>rvav-tier/gold:soft</mono>.

templates.sheetLead: VM forms offer it in their template picker, to the projects and environments below.
templates.linkedNote: Clone its VMs from the vCenter template's current snapshot, unless the blueprint says otherwise. Not for content library items; the VMs keep the template's disk size.
templates.cloudbaseInitNote: The template has cloudbase-init with its VMware GuestInfo service. rvav gives its VMs their name, network, user and user data through guestinfo instead of a customization specification.
templates.userDataLinuxHint: Merged with the item's. A Go template, as a blueprint's: print inputs through json. Empty for none.
templates.userDataWindowsHint: Run before the item's: #ps1_sysnative, rem cmd or #cloud-config. A Go template, as a blueprint's. Empty for none.
templates.title: VM templates
templates.panelLead: What VM forms offer in their template picker, and to which projects.
templates.emptyBody: Blueprints name a vCenter template themselves until you add templates for their pickers.
templates.removeLead: VM forms stop offering <mono>{{key}}</mono> in their template picker.
templates.removeConsequences: Offered to {{offers}}. A blueprint that names its own template keeps it, and VMs built from this one aren't changed.

sizes.sheetLead: VM forms offer it in their size picker, to the projects and environments below.
sizes.title: Sizes
sizes.panelLead: What VM forms offer in their size picker: vCPU, memory and system disk.
sizes.emptyBody: Blueprints set their own vCPU and memory until you add sizes for their pickers.
sizes.removeLead: VM forms stop offering <mono>{{key}}</mono> in their size picker.
sizes.removeConsequences: Offered to {{offers}}. A blueprint that sets its own size keeps it, and VMs of this size aren't changed.

networks.sheetLead: A mapping by hand wins over EfficientIP's until it is removed.
networks.title: Network mappings
networks.panelLead: EfficientIP's subnets come with their vCenter network in the sync; map a network by hand when EfficientIP doesn't say. A network with IP ranges takes its addresses from them.
networks.emptyBody: The EfficientIP sync maps the networks it knows. Map one by hand when it doesn't.
networks.removeLead: Its subnet {{subnet}}, set by hand, stops applying.
networks.removeConsequences: The next EfficientIP sync brings back EfficientIP's subnet for the network, if it has one. VMs already on the network keep their addresses.

inventory.clusterHeld: , {{reserved}} GB of it held for VMs not built yet

host.maintenance: In {{cluster}}, {{free}} of {{total}} GB memory free, in maintenance
host.disconnected: In {{cluster}}, {{free}} of {{total}} GB memory free, disconnected

datastoreCluster.on: {{free}} of {{capacity}} GB free on {{datastores}}, Storage DRS on
datastoreCluster.off: {{free}} of {{capacity}} GB free on {{datastores}}, Storage DRS off

inventory.name: Name
inventory.title: vCenter objects
inventory.lead: The clusters, hosts, resource pools, datastores, datastore clusters and networks the last inventory sync read. Placement rules name them, and blueprints' constraints choose by their vSphere tags, written category/tag.
inventory.nothingMatchesBody: No vCenter object has that name or tag.
inventory.emptyBody: The inventory sync lists them once a vCenter is connected.

ipRanges.sheetLead: VMs on the network take their addresses from its ranges instead of EfficientIP. rvav writes no DNS records for them.
ipRanges.name: Name
ipRanges.held_one: A VM holds {{count}} address from this range: its vCenter, network, subnet and gateway stay as they are.
ipRanges.held_other: VMs hold {{count}} addresses from this range: its vCenter, network, subnet and gateway stay as they are.
ipRanges.networkHint: A port group or an NSX segment's
ipRanges.excludedHint: One address or span per line, such as 10.51.0.50-10.51.0.59: never given.
ipRanges.searchDomainsHint: Comma-separated, searched after the VM's own domain
ipRanges.dnsDomainHint: The domain VMs are named in; empty: the blueprint's. rvav creates no DNS records in it.
ipRanges.addressesLead: {{network}} in {{vcenter}}. rvav gives an address back when its VM or adapter goes.
ipRanges.noneGivenBody: The network's next VM gets the range's first free address.

reconcile.title: Reconcile the IP ranges
reconcile.lead: Compares the ranges with what VMs hold. Nothing changes unless you give an address back.
reconcile.intro: It lists the addresses given to VMs rvav no longer has, such as an unregistered VM's, and the vCenter VMs on an address of a range that didn't give it to them.
reconcile.cleanBody: Every address given belongs to a VM rvav has, and no vCenter VM is on an address its range didn't give it.
reconcile.orphans: Addresses of VMs rvav no longer has
reconcile.unallocated: VMs on an address their range didn't give
reconcile.unallocatedLead: Exclude the address from its range, or move the VM, so that the range never gives it to another VM.
reconcile.giveBackLead: No deployment has {{hostname}} any more: the range can give the address to its next VM.
reconcile.giveBackConsequences: If the VM still runs on this address in vCenter, exclude the address from the range instead.

ipRanges.title: IP ranges
ipRanges.lead: Addresses rvav gives VMs itself, on networks EfficientIP doesn't manage: a network with a range takes its new VMs' addresses from it. rvav creates no DNS records for them.
ipRanges.emptyBody: Every network takes its VMs' addresses from EfficientIP. Add a range for a network EfficientIP doesn't manage.
ipRanges.removeHeld_one: A VM holds {{count}} address from it: delete it, or move its adapter, first.
ipRanges.removeHeld_other: VMs hold {{count}} addresses from it: delete them, or move their adapters, first.
ipRanges.removeFree: When it is the network's last range, the network's new VMs take their addresses from EfficientIP again.
